A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEC research and vision backbone. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison despite substantial expansion and restructuring in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification, COCO detection and segmentation, ADE20K segmentation, ablation and clustering-visualization results.

after.justification: v2 reports original vision experiments plus SEC-based LLaVA evaluations, self-supervised training results and additional sensitivity and token-merging analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds interleaved grouping and attentive pooling to compress visual tokens for a vision-language connector, extending v1's within-cluster vision attention (Section 3.2, Equations 5–6). SECViT stage depths and some attention-head counts also change, and an XL configuration is introduced (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 12).

E1.justification: ImageNet-1K, COCO and ADE20K coverage is retained. v2 adds visual-question-answering and multimodal-understanding evaluations, including TextVQA, GQA, VQAv2, POPE, MME, MMB and MM-Vet (Tables 8–10), substantially extending the represented tasks.

E2.justification: The strict backbone comparison changes from Swin/FasterViT to Swin/DeiT and adds explicit EViT comparisons (v1 Table 2; v2 Tables 1–2). Vision benchmark tables introduce comparators including RMT and MLLA. New multimodal comparisons evaluate MLP, Resampler, pooling, EViT and several complete MLLMs.

E3.justification: New protocols include 800-epoch masked-image pretraining and MLLM evaluations varying language-model size and visual-token budget. SECViT model configurations are revised and extended to XL. ADE20K FLOP measurement for the tiny-model group changes from 512×512 to 512×2048; the established vision training schedules largely remain.

E4.justification: v1's LCE, CPE, convolutional-stem and CSWin-attention ablations are removed. v2 replaces the classification-only cluster-count sweep with token-per-cluster tests covering throughput and dense prediction, adds MLLM token-budget and interleaved-versus-sequential merging analyses (Tables 11, 14–15), and adds Grad-CAM and complex-scene visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results without documented repeated-run counts, seed replication, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized score differences are not uncertainty estimates; v2's average inference times do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: SECViT-S's ImageNet entry changes from 84.2% at 4.4G FLOPs to 84.3% at 4.6G under a revised architecture (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 4). COCO and ADE20K entries also change. v2 adds XL's 86.3% classification result, self-supervised results and extensive multimodal accuracy/timing results. These include changed-setting and newly reported results.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions of interleaved token groups and pooled-query attention for the connector (Equations 5–6). The shared cosine-similarity and sorting construction remains substantively unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1's principal contribution is efficient semantic clustering for a general vision backbone. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden this contribution to vision-language connectors, claiming that SEC accelerates MLLMs while maintaining or improving performance. The original single-pass, balanced-clustering claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations distinguishing similarity-based clustering from importance-based pruning and relating feature-map preservation to dense prediction (Section 3.3). It interprets failures from overly small clusters and sequential token merging. Meanwhile, v1 Appendix C's explicit limitation concerning larger models and datasets such as ImageNet-21K is removed.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's in-PDF SECA implementation and promised code-release URL, and stops documenting LCE's kernel, EMA and some segmentation optimizer details. Most vision training recipes remain, while architecture specifications and XL settings are added or revised. These omissions establish reduced documentation, without establishing that the underlying implementation choices were discontinued.

R1.justification: v2 adds a vision-language-connector related-work discussion covering works such as LLaVA, Honeybee and Perceiver, and explicitly positions SEC against EViT pruning. References also introduce newer vision and self-supervised methods, while v1's ToMe-based justification and FasterViT comparison disappear. The research positioning extends substantially beyond vision-backbone grouping.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized from separate vision-task subsections into vision-model and MLLM sections. v2 adds a dedicated EViT discussion, condenses existing architecture and experiment prose, and restructures the appendices by merging architecture/settings material and replacing the limitations, impact and code sections with additional results.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document to two columns and substantially restructures the benchmark tables. Figure 2 gains a connector comparison plot, and Figure 3 is redrawn to include the multimodal pathway. Figure 4 rearranges existing clustering examples and adds Grad-CAM; Figure 5 adds complex scenes. Numerous new experimental tables accompany these changes.

improvement.justification: v2's direct DeiT/EViT comparisons and richer cluster-size and merging analyses provide clearer evidence about where SEC helps and fails than v1's backbone-focused evaluation. The net gain is limited by removing the code listing and component ablations, sparse documentation of MLLM training, and numerical inconsistencies: Table 11 reports 47.7 mIoU with a −0.5 difference from 47.2. These tradeoffs prevent the substantial expansion from establishing a major overall quality improvement.
